doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Lunch gigs with George Coleman Jr. and Gloria Coleman; Bradley's and Rufus Reid
summary: Playing Thursday and Friday lunchtimes at the Film Center, hearing trios at Bradley's, studying with Rufus Reid, then leaving fashion for a Swiss gig in early 1995.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Son. And his mother, who passed away recently in Philadelphia. A wonderful piano player. But they kind of took me in and it was just really a beautiful experience. I think I did that for like a year even, just playing there a couple of times a week, and it was just like a way to get your feet wet. It was a fun gig you know, it was just for people having coffee before they went to the movie. I didn’t care you know what I mean? You just want to play and get out there. And then at night if I could afford it I’d go to Bradley’s. And my teacher was Rufus Reid at the time.
So I’d go down to see Rufus and the piano players and trios that played at Bradley’s. You know I could walk there. It was wonderful. It was a great time.
And you’re absorbing just watching these people, how they played the gig and how they behaved and all that good stuff.

Yeah. Basically. Pretty much. And then after eight months I had a gig in Switzerland so I quit my day job, and that was early ’95. And actually they offered me a full time job in fashion with commission and all. I could have actually gone down this whole other road in New York. I’d actually been a musician in Sydney and then just gone to New York and then I could have woooh, I could have made money, I could have done, it was kind of like almost too easy do you know what I mean? Plus I do — that’s not my love. I like nice clothes, who doesn’t? But it’s like that’s not a passion at all. So I said no thank you and I just decided to try to figure it out.
